source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 10.

sections.heading: 1. Living and Non-living
points: Things are grouped as **living** (plants, animals, microbes) and **non-living** (stone, water, chair).
Living things show a set of **characteristics (life processes)**; non-living things do not show all of them.
Some non-living things show one feature (a car moves, a river flows) but **not all** life characteristics — so they are non-living.

sections.heading: 2. Characteristics of Living Things
points: **Nutrition** — need **food** for energy and growth (plants make their own by **photosynthesis**; animals depend on others).
**Respiration** — take in oxygen (or exchange gases) to release energy from food.
**Growth** — increase in size over time.
**Movement** — living things move (animals move place to place; plants show movement, e.g. towards light).
**Response to stimuli** — react to changes (a **stimulus**), e.g. touch-me-not (Mimosa) folds leaves.
**Excretion** — remove waste from the body.
**Reproduction** — produce young ones of their own kind.
All living things eventually have a **life span / life cycle** (are born, grow, and die).

sections.heading: 3. Stimulus and Response
points: A **stimulus** = a change in the surroundings that causes a reaction.
A **response** = the reaction of the organism.
Examples: pupils narrowing in bright light; roots growing towards water; leaves moving towards sunlight.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Characteristics of life: nutrition, respiration, growth, movement, response to stimuli, excretion, reproduction, life span.
Plants make food by photosynthesis; animals depend on others.
Stimulus = change in surroundings; response = the reaction.
A car/river shows one feature (movement/flow) but not all → non-living.
Reproduction = producing more of one's own kind.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **A single feature (like movement) does not make a thing living** — living things show ALL the characteristics together.
**Plants do move and respond** (e.g. towards light; Mimosa leaves fold) — movement is not limited to animals.
**Respiration** (releasing energy from food) is different from mere breathing.
Reproduction ensures the **species continues**, even though individuals die.
